mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.1%) compresses risk-free rates, increasing the present value of future equity cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%, or the Rank IC over 12 months is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 10.0%, it signals a severe economic contraction that triggers a policy response, leading to a rebound in equity valuations as the market prices in eventual recovery, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 10.0, or the average return in such periods is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based collapse in consumer and business spending, which is a leading indicator of a severe recession. This triggers a flight to safety and then a policy response, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market anticipates stimulus.
failure_condition: The interaction term (HOUST and RSAFS both declining) fails to predict positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.04 over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply shock regime (INDPRO < 95.0), the contraction in industrial output leads to a loss of confidence in the economy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market prices in prolonged economic weakness.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0, or the Rank IC for INDPRO < 95.0 is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in monthly payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a weakening labor market, which typically leads to a reduction in consumer spending and a subsequent decline in corporate earnings, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS declines, or the Rank IC over 12 months is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1200.0 (thousands of units), it signals a contraction in the housing sector, which is a key component of consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the market reacts to the weak data.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 1200.0, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a severe labor market deterioration, which is a leading indicator of a deep recession. This triggers a policy response and a subsequent market rebound, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction (PAYEMS decline and UNRATE rise) fails to predict positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.04.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is at or below 0.05%, it signals the zero lower bound, limiting the Federal Reserve's ability to cut rates further, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the market prices in a lack of monetary stimulus.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS <= 0.05, or the Rank IC over 12 months is below 0.02.
